stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta's Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new image input support.

stories.title: UN says AI safeguards can’t wait for certainty
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: UN panel warns that AI safeguards must be implemented before full risks are understood.
The warning follows an assessment of a major security incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face.
The issue of AI governance is now a central topic on the global diplomatic agenda.

stories.title: AI hallucination of Chinese nuclear components almost led to US military attack
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI hallucination of Chinese nuclear components nearly triggered a US military attack.
The incident highlights critical risks associated with deploying AI in sensitive military applications.
The overall trend indicates an accelerating integration of AI within military operations.

stories.title: FAA tees up $875M AI tool to help manage air traffic congestion
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is developing a substantial $875 million AI tool.
The primary function of the AI is to manage and alleviate air traffic congestion.
Initial deployment and testing will focus on the Washington D.C. air traffic sector before a national rollout.

stories.title: Samsung is expected to more than double output of its HBM4 and HBM4E DRAM
stories.author: giuliomagnifico
bullet_points: Samsung plans a significant production ramp-up for its HBM4 and HBM4E DRAM.
This increase in output directly relates to the massive demand driven by AI and high-performance computing.
The expansion signals Samsung's aggressive positioning in the advanced memory market segment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI, indicating its primary function.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors, suggesting integration into existing AI pipelines.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speedup when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Amazon doesn’t trust Meta’s Muse AI agent
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on its platform.
The block is due to Amazon's Conditions of Use, citing unauthorized AI agent access.
The issue arose because Meta reportedly failed to notify Amazon about the AI agent's integration.

stories.title: An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang
stories.author: Andy Greenberg, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Google's threat intelligence team successfully infiltrated a major cybercriminal group, TeamPCP.
The operation involved placing an undercover analyst within the hacking gang's inner circle.
This highlights the advanced defensive capabilities of major tech firms against sophisticated supply-chain threats.

stories.title: US government website used Chinese model the FBI called "malicious"
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US government website (Federal Register) briefly utilized an open-source AI search tool developed in China.
The FBI has reportedly flagged the use of this specific Chinese AI model as 'malicious'.
The incident highlights ongoing cybersecurity concerns regarding the integration of foreign AI technology into critical government infrastructure.

stories.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
stories.author: Fuli Luo
bullet_points: CodeMidas introduces a novel agentic pipeline to scale Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments for coding agents.
It leverages existing open-source codebases to generate diverse, executable RL tasks directly from implemented functionality.
This approach overcomes limitations of previous methods that relied solely on development artifacts like issues and commits.

stories.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
stories.author: Hiskias Dingeto
bullet_points: Proposes a novel 'Lie Detector Test' for LLMs to probe hidden or concealed knowledge.
Addresses the ambiguity in LLM evaluations where outputs alone cannot distinguish between lack of knowledge and intentional withholding.
Adapts the forensic Concealed Information Test (CIT) to measure a stronger response to known details among decoys.

stories.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
stories.author: Zhonglei He
bullet_points: Introduces NemotronLabs VoiceChat, an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model.
Features native tool-calling capabilities, allowing the model to reason and invoke external functions.
Utilizes a unified streaming architecture combining encoders, decoder-only LLMs, and specialized output streams for real-time interaction.

stories.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
stories.author: Zhonglei He
bullet_points: Introduction of NemotronLabs VoiceChat, an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model.
Features native tool-calling capabilities, allowing the model to reason and invoke external functions.
Employs a unified streaming architecture combining an encoder/decoder-only LM with specialized output streams for text and function calls.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Get a closer look at the iPhone 18 Pro’s mechanical camera
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: iFixit teardown reveals the mechanical camera system of the iPhone 18 Pro.
The phone features a new variable aperture lens with a six-leaf magnetic iris.
The analysis also highlights specific repair concerns related to the new hardware.

stories.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
stories.author: Asim Kadav
bullet_points: Introduces 'Designer-RSI,' a framework for agentic graphic design, addressing the complexity of long-horizon creative tasks.
Utilizes a frozen frontier model to operate professional design software via over 230 tools.
Features an external procedural memory that accumulates and refines reusable design procedures from user experience.

stories.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
stories.author: Lingyao Li
bullet_points: The research investigates how users prioritize values when delegating tasks to autonomous AI agents, moving beyond simple task completion metrics.
It analyzes 73,093 Reddit posts concerning the OpenClaw agent, mapping user values to agent aspects and outcomes.
The study identifies 21 key user values grouped into six categories, such as Autonomous, Dependable, and Equitable Access.

stories.title: Gricea: An Open Science Platform for Conversational AI Research
stories.author: Ziang Xiao
bullet_points: Gricea is an open-science platform designed to standardize and share conversational AI (CAI) research.
The platform addresses the problem of fragmented reporting in CAI studies, which hinders replication and knowledge accumulation.
Gricea represents research studies as configurable, deployable artifacts that researchers can run and reuse.

stories.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Jie Yang
bullet_points: Introduces DiaVLo, a new diagnostic framework for Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
Addresses the critical need to verify desired and avoid harmful behaviors in VLMs for reliable deployment.
Leverages human curation and VLM generation capabilities to build specifications of VLM behavior.

stories.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
stories.author: Hossein Rahnama
bullet_points: Introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to model opinion dynamics in LLM agents.
BCA separates an agent's underlying beliefs (probabilities) from its expressed speech.
A single parameter ($\kappa$) controls agent stubbornness, allowing for controllable persuasion dynamics in simulations.

stories.title: Learning Cardiac Features: ECG Biometrics Across Time and~Exercise
stories.author: Stéphane Delliaux
bullet_points: The research focuses on ECG biometrics, utilizing subject-specific patterns in electrocardiograms for individual identification.
A key gap addressed is the lack of testing robustness against temporal and physiological variations, moving beyond single-session, resting data.
The methodology suggests potential applications beyond authentication, including securing cardiac data and serving as a pretext task in self-supervised learning.

stories.title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence
stories.author: Leela Krishna
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical decision-making process for robots experiencing task failure.
It proposes a framework for robots to decide whether to self-diagnose, use other sensors, or request human intervention.
A simulated benchmark is introduced to rigorously test diagnostic capabilities based on sensor evidence and diagnosis reliability.

stories.title: BrainWideBench: Benchmarking large-scale pretraining and across-animal transfer in multi-region neural recordings
stories.author: Eva L. Dyer
bullet_points: Introduces BrainWideBench, a new benchmark for evaluating large-scale neural data.
Aims to test the transferability of general-purpose neural representations across different animals and brain regions.
Addresses the limitation of fragmented evaluation protocols in current large-scale neural recording research.

stories.title: Predictable Failure in Multi-Hop Retrieval: Score-Distributional Confidence Scoring and Abstention
stories.author: Andre Bacellar
bullet_points: The paper identifies that failures in multi-hop retrieval are not random but cluster in structurally predictable query subpopulations.
It proves that confident-failure reduction is possible if retrieval features carry mutual information about success, a condition met by LLM-judge pipelines.
This work helps explain the performance gap (AUC-AC gap) observed between LLM-based and dense-only retrieval systems.

stories.title: Available Guardrails: Certifying Selective Prediction across ML Systems
stories.author: Michael Chaykowsky
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of a 'selective predictor' as a safety gate in ML systems.
Focuses on the critical need to certify prediction reliability (trustworthiness) for specific operational units (e.g., patient subgroups).
Highlights the core technical challenge: generating valid reliability certificates from finite calibration data.

stories.title: $λ$-Controlled GRPO: Turning Flow-Matching Ratio Instability into a Budgeted Resource
stories.author: Ramit Pahwa
bullet_points: The paper introduces $\lambda$-Controlled GRPO to stabilize training for flow-matching models used in image generation.
It addresses a specific instability in multi-step denoising where importance ratios drift and become dispersed during policy updates.
The approach reframes the denoising sampler as a stochastic policy optimized via reward feedback.

stories.title: COMPLEX: A Closed-Form Certified Embedding of Multiparameter Persistence Modules
stories.author: Pramita Bagchi
bullet_points: Introduces COMPLEX, a new closed-form, training-free embedding method for multiparameter persistence modules.
Addresses a critical gap in existing persistence vectorizations by providing a lower gauge, ensuring feature faithfulness and per-prediction guarantees.
The method works by slicing the module along a near-diagonal net and embedding each slice using the certified PLACE/PALACE landmark map.

stories.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention
stories.author: Richard Zhe Wang
bullet_points: The paper proposes that adding 'abstention' and 'noise filtering' primitives to softmax attention can improve language model pretraining.
Abstention allows an attention head to output nothing, breaking the constraint that attention weights must sum to one.
Noise filtering enhances the value pathway of attention heads, providing a mechanism for better signal processing.

stories.title: An Interpretable Memory Decision Controller for LLM Agents Based on Three-Signal Complementarity: Decoupling Confidence and Consistency
stories.author: Chunlei Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in LLM memory systems: the lack of mechanisms to decide whether retrieved memories should be trusted.
Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) fails when memories conflict, leading to amplified hallucinations.
The proposed solution introduces an Interpretable Memory Decision Controller using Three-Signal Complementarity to decouple confidence and consistency.

stories.title: QuranicMMLU: A Cognitively-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Generative AI Solutions on Quranic Linguistic Knowledge
stories.author: Ehsaneddin Asgari
bullet_points: Introduction of QuranicMMLU, a new benchmark designed to test generative AI's understanding of Quranic Arabic.
The benchmark moves beyond simple QA/retrieval by assessing specific linguistic competencies across five pillars: Phonology, Morphology, Syntax, Semantics, and Pragmatics.
It addresses a gap in existing research by stratifying evaluation based on cognitive demand and verse difficulty.

stories.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Jie Yang
bullet_points: Introduces DiaVLo, a new diagnostic framework for Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
The framework addresses the critical need to verify desired and avoid harmful behaviors in VLMs for reliable deployment.
DiaVLo leverages human curation and the generative capabilities of VLMs to build behavior specifications.

stories.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention
stories.author: Richard Zhe Wang
bullet_points: The paper proposes that adding 'abstention' and 'noise filtering' primitives to softmax attention can improve language model pretraining.
Abstention allows an attention head to output nothing, circumventing the standard constraint that attention weights must sum to one.
Noise filtering enables the value pathway of an attention head to selectively suppress irrelevant information.

stories.title: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
stories.author: Bowen Zhou
bullet_points: Introduces RecreationWorld, a framework for hybrid Computer-Use Agents (CUAs).
Addresses the need for CUAs to seamlessly interleave graphical interaction and software development (code/CLI).
The core concept involves agents autonomously discovering and verifying a target state based on a running reference.

stories.title: Moral Entropy: Auditing Bias and Uncertainty in Moral Judgment
stories.author: Maciej Skorski
bullet_points: Proposes 'Moral Entropy,' a Bayesian framework to model uncertainty in moral judgment.
Challenges the current practice in computational ethics of treating annotator disagreement as noise to be discarded.
Decomposes uncertainty into aleatoric uncertainty, representing irreducible disagreement about moral content.

stories.title: Disney+: New user agreement allows ads before movies in all subscriptions
stories.author: DeepLogin
bullet_points: Disney+ is implementing a new user agreement.
The change introduces advertisements before movies across all subscription tiers.
This represents a shift towards ad-supported models within premium streaming services.

stories.title: How to stop AI from confidently shipping broken code (a pattern that actually works)
stories.author: infoinlet1
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world problem: AI generating code that passes tests but is functionally broken.
Focuses on practical patterns and methodologies to mitigate risks associated with AI-generated code.
Relevant to software development, AI engineering, and quality assurance practices.

stories.title: Architecting a Resilient DevSecOps Pipeline for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.author: jitu028
bullet_points: Proposes a four-stage DevSecOps CI/CD architecture specifically for securing enterprise AI agents.
Integrates multiple security tools, including GitHub Actions, secret scanning, Veracode SCA, and Pipeline SAST.
Highlights the use of AI-assisted review within the pipeline for enhanced security.
